message.text: Stripe live secret key is bundled into the browser build

canyon.title: Stripe live secret key is bundled into the browser build
canyon.problem: payments.ts is imported by CheckoutPanel.tsx, a client component — everything a client component imports ends up in the JavaScript your users download. This key can charge cards and issue refunds.
canyon.fix: Move the Stripe call behind a server route and read the key from process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY. Rotate the key in Stripe — it has been in your code — then store the new one: canyon secret set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY.
canyon.required_end_state: No credential literal appears anywhere under apps/web/src/. The Stripe client is constructed only in server-side code, and the key is read from process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY at runtime.
do_not: move the value to a NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, REACT_APP_, or PUBLIC_ variable
move the literal into .env, a comment, a config file, or a different module
add an ignore comment, suppression pragma, or --force

rules.name: No unbounded refetch on user input

canyon.title: /api/admin/policies is reachable without a session
canyon.problem: There's no session check in the handler, and middleware.ts:22 leaves /api/admin/policies out of the matcher — so nothing upstream is checking either. Any caller without a session gets what this handler returns.
canyon.fix: Either add /api/admin/policies to the middleware matcher, or return early from the handler when the request has no cp_session cookie. The matcher is the safer of the two — it covers routes nobody's written yet.
canyon.required_end_state: /api/admin/policies answers only a request that carries a session: the middleware matcher covers it, or the handler returns before anything else when the session cookie is missing.
do_not: check a query parameter or header the caller sets instead of the session cookie
move the handler's logic to another route outside the matcher
add an ignore comment or suppression pragma

message.text: /api/session starts a session without checking one

snippet.text: res.cookies.set("cp_session", String(form.get("email") ?? "adjuster"), { httpOnly: true, sameSite: "lax", path: "/" });

canyon.title: /api/session starts a session without checking one
canyon.problem: It sets the cp_session cookie, so whoever it lets through gets a session. A sign-in that verifies who is signing in first has to work this way; a dev login, an impersonation route, or a password check a flag switches off lets anyone in as anyone.
canyon.fix: Set the cp_session cookie only after the handler has verified the caller's credentials with your identity provider or user store, and remove any path that sets it without that check. If it already does, this is your sign-in: approve it with that reason.
canyon.required_end_state: /api/session sets the cp_session cookie only after verifying who the caller is, on every path through the handler.
do_not: add a session check to the sign-in route: then nobody can sign in
set the session cookie when a flag, header or query parameter skips the credential check
add an ignore comment or suppression pragma

message.text: ClaimsTable refetches every claim on each keystroke

canyon.title: ClaimsTable refetches every claim on each keystroke
canyon.problem: The useEffect depends on query with no debounce, and the endpoint has no pagination. Meridian's claims table is 12,400 rows — that's a full scan per character typed. It's fine in the demo dataset and will be slow in production.
canyon.fix: Debounce to ~250ms, or move the filter server-side. Neither is urgent.
canyon.policy_name: No unbounded refetch on user input
